You can use graph measures to lock an aggregation to a key in order to perform complex aggregations without overcounting. Measure expressions can include the following:

  • Aggregate function calls
  • Expressions within aggregate functions
  • Conditional logic within aggregate functions
  • Conditional distinct counting
  • Scalar operations and expressions outside of aggregate functions
  • Combinations of measures wrapped in the AGG function

To query measures, you transform your graph into a flattened table by using the GRAPH_EXPAND TVF, and then query measures in that table with the AGG function. The GRAPH_EXPAND function now supports multiple fact tables. To view the output schema of the GRAPH_EXPAND function, use the BQ.SHOW_GRAPH_EXPAND_SCHEMA system procedure.

You can define extensions in the OPTIONS clause of the labels and properties in your graphs, which are string pairs that represent custom metadata for natural language querying.

Measures and graphs are supported in Data Studio through the BigQuery connector. Measures and graphs are also automatically cataloged in Knowledge Catalog, which makes them searchable by natural language or domain synonyms.

These features are generally available (GA).

Lakehouse supports the following remote catalog providers for cross-cloud data access. This feature is generally available (GA).

  • Databricks Unity Catalog on Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
  • AWS Glue Data Catalog on AWS
  • Snowflake Horizon Catalog on AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Workday Data Lake on AWS or Google Cloud

This feature lets you configure federated catalog endpoints to synchronize catalog metadata and query Apache Iceberg tables in remote catalogs directly from Google Cloud using BigQuery, Managed Service for Apache Spark, and Apache Spark without migrating data or building complex ETL pipelines. You can route background metadata refresh and queries over the public internet or privately over Cross-Cloud Interconnect, and protect cross-cloud data access with VPC Service Controls service perimeters. For Databricks Unity Catalog, you can also use user identity federation to propagate end-user identities on queries for permission enforcement and audit logging.

For more information, see About cross-cloud data access, Query remote data, and Use VPC Service Controls with federated catalog endpoints.

BigQuery offers TimesFM 3.0, a built-in time series forecasting model that implements Google Research's open source TimesFM model. You can use TimesFM 3.0 with the following functions:

  • Use AI.FORECAST to perform time series forecasting. In addition to univariate forecasting, you can now perform multivariate forecasting that predicts values for multiple time series based on historical values and additional covariates.
  • Use AI.EVALUATE to perform univariate time series evaluation.
  • Use AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES to perform univariate time series anomaly detection.

Conversational analytics in BigQuery also supports using TimesFM 3.0 with these functions.

To try using the TimesFM 3.0 model for multivariate forecasting with the AI.FORECAST function, see Forecast a single time series with a TimesFM multivariate model and Forecast multiple time series with a TimesFM multivariate model.

The TimesFM 3.0 model is in Preview.

updates.text: The BigQuery Data Transfer Service MCP server is now Generally Available (GA).

updates.html: You can now write the output rows produced by BigQuery continuous queries directly into Apache Iceberg managed tables. This lets you continuously process streaming data from BigQuery and write it into your open-format lakehouse by using an INSERT DML statement.

updates.html: In the BigQuery Studio query editor, the Query results table now keeps the row numbers visible on the left as you scroll horizontally. This helps you maintain context and track data across wide tables. This feature is generally available (GA).

updates.html:
You can now publish a BigQuery data agent in Gemini Enterprise by registering the agent with Agent Registry and importing it using default Google-managed credentials. When BigQuery and Gemini Enterprise are in the same Google Cloud project and configured with a matching Agent Gateway region, you don't need to manually copy the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) JSON card or configure OAuth client credentials.

These features are in Preview.

updates.html:
Lakehouse now supports Workday Data Lake as a remote catalog provider for cross-cloud data access (Preview). You can configure federated catalogs to query data stored in Workday Data Lake directly from Google Cloud using BigQuery or Apache Spark without migrating data or building complex ETL pipelines.

For more information, see Set up cross-cloud connection for Workday Data Lake.
